segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Hey, can you look at the renewal queue with me for North Ridge Plastics? I pulled it from the CRM and it looks odd.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Yeah, one sec. That's the calibration tracking workspace, right? Twenty-eight seats and the gauge import add-on?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yep. Their agreement ended July 31, so we're already two weeks past it, and I don't see any call notes, emails, or tasks from us about carrying on. Like, nobody has talked to Dana or their plant ops team about renewing, extending, anything. The billing tool still shows them active because the invoice run is monthly, but contractually we're past the end date with no customer conversation.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Oh, that's not good. I see the same thing. Last activity was June 18, support ticket on certificate formatting, then nothing from sales. No renewal quote attached either.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Right, and they were supposed to add six seats for the second shift in September. If we go to them now, it can't sound like we forgot, but we need to be clear on access and dates.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Agreed. Do we have pricing locked from the old order form? It says $31,200 annual, net 30, auto-renew unchecked.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Pricing sheet has them at $93 per seat per month, plus $4,800 for the add-on. If we hold that and add six seats, new annual is $38,? wait, $38,016 before tax.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Deal desk will want a bridge note. Maybe propose a 12-month term from August 1 through July 31 next year, so there's no weird partial month.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah. I'll send Dana a short note asking for 20 minutes tomorrow, and I'll own that we need to align the renewal paperwork and added seats. No blame, no drama.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Good. Attach the quote after she replies. Also check with finance on whether August usage should be invoiced under the renewal or as a separate catch-up line.
